Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the QBR last week. As we prep for our renewal discussion with procurement later this month, finance asked for a tighter reconciliation of our token spend vs. feature usage. I've attached the CSV export of our account for the last 90 days — you'll see some spikes around the mobile preview feature (Sep 2–4).

Two asks:
- Can you confirm how Redwood is accounting for prefix tokens vs. generated tokens for embeddings and chat? We're trying to reconcile what shows up in our internal billing.
- We ran a quick prefilling experiment (server-side prompt prefill) that looks like it reduced average prompt length by ~18% across the product. Can you run a short ROI recap that shows estimated monthly savings if we adopt prefill across all endpoints?

Bradley (cc) will be on point from engineering if you need log samples. Ideally we get the reconciliation + ROI before the renewal meeting on Sep 22.

Appreciate it —
Elena Morris
Head of Platform
ClearWave AI

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Consumption reconciliation + prefill efficiency recap

Elena —

Got the export, thank you. I pulled an initial pass and here are the headline items (will follow with a short doc and a token-level table by EOD Monday):

1) Token accounting: Redwood reports three token categories in the billing export: prefix (incoming prompt tokens), generation (model output), and system/meta (tracing and vectorization overhead). For embeddings calls we surface the prompt tokens associated with each vectorization request as prefix tokens; generation is zero for pure embeddings. I'll attach the token-level mapping for your CSV so you can match rows.

2) Prefill ROI: based on the sample you ran (18% average prompt length reduction), conservative estimate is a 13–15% monthly token cost savings once prefill is applied across chat and completion endpoints (variance depends on message lengths and KV-cache hit rate). Assumptions: same request rate, no change to response size.

3) Spikes: the Sep 2–4 increase aligns with a staging job that accidentally used the higher-temperature debug model (higher token expansion). Bradley — if you can confirm the job id I can tag the rows.

Next steps I'm proposing:
- Soojin/Redwood: deliver a one-page ROI recap + a CSV with token breakdown by route (Mon, 14 Sep).
- Karthik: can we prepare two proposal options for procurement (pilot addendum + burst credits vs. commit uplift)?
- Monica: ops to confirm whether the prefilling approach needs an SLA change (latency expectations).

Happy to hop on a 30m call next Tue/Wed.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Team — quick pricing sketch to surface options before the call:

Option A — Commit uplift: +30% committed tokens (12-month), no change to per-token rates, includes 5% committed discount on overage. Rationale: reduces unit cost and covers expected growth.

Option B — Pilot + bridge credits: 8-week prefill pilot, Redwood provides 50k burst credits and 10% credit on token usage for the pilot period. Post-pilot, we evaluate uplift vs. conversion to commit.

Operational notes: commit changes require procurement notice ~10 business days; pilot can start within 48 hours of addendum signature. I'll attach a quick pricing options spreadsheet.

—Karthik

Elena — ops note from the early log samples Bradley sent:

- We saw a 250ms median latency increase on Sep 3 correlating with the debug-model runs. The per-request token expansion (larger generated token sizes) accounts for most of the cost delta in the export.
- Prefill reduces prompt-side tokens but can increase server-side CPU for some pipelines depending on where the prefill happens (client vs. gateway). Recommend running the pilot with prefill executed at the gateway to maximize cache hits.

Quick checklist for the pilot:
- Redwood to enable gateway prefill flag for your account (no infra changes needed).
- Engineering (Bradley) to share a small sample of requests for baseline latency comparison (we'll keep it scoped to 2 endpoints).
- CS (Monica) to monitor latency, error-rate, and token delta daily.

I'll set up the monitoring dashboard and share access before the pilot.

Monica Patel
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
